title: Isolation of Microglia from Mouse or Human Tissue
protocol: Aliquot 5 mL of Enzyme Digestion Mix into 15 mL tubes and weigh the tubes.
Perform saline transcardiac perfusion (see Note).
Dissect the brain region of interest.
Chop up the brain tissue with razor blades on ice.
Place chopped-up tissue in cold enzyme digestion mix on ice.
Place brain samples in a 37°C water bath for 15 min.
Agitate samples every 5 min during the incubation period.
Avoid inverting tubes to prevent tissue from becoming stuck near the lid of 15 ml tubes.
Dissociate tissue to a single-cell suspension over three separate flame-polished Pasteur pipets, starting with pipet #1, then #2, and finally #3.
Pipette up and down 20 times with each pipet.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes after using the first pipet before proceeding to the next pipet.
Agitate tubes every 5 minutes during the incubation period by pipetting up and down 20 times.
Pipette aggregated tissue until all tissue moves freely into the Pasteur pipet.
Prepare the 30% and 70% percoll solutions after using the first pipet, ensuring they are at approximately 20°C to 25°C.
Filter samples into fresh 15 mL tubes.
Place 70 μm nylon filters on top of fresh 15 mL tubes.
Pre-wet each filter with 1 mL of HBSS (with calcium/magnesium).
Add cell suspension over the pre-wet area on each filter.
Rinse old 15 mL tubes with 2 mL of HBSS (with calcium/magnesium) and pipette up and down to mix.
Add the mixture over the filter.
Fill new tubes to 15 mL with HBSS (with calcium/magnesium).
Centrifuge samples for 10 minutes at 300 × g, 4°C, max acceleration, half brake.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cell suspension carefully with 3,100 μL of ice-cold 1X PBS and transfer to a fresh 15 mL tube.
Add 900 μL of cold Debris Removal Solution.
Mix well by pipetting 10 times slowly up and down.
Slowly layer 4 mL of 1X PBS on top, creating a visible gradient.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at maximum speed (at least 3,000 × g), 4°C, with max acceleration and brake.
Remove the top two layers.
Fill up to 14 mL with ice cold 1X PBS.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 1,000 × g, 4°C, with max acceleration and brake.
Aspirate the supernatant from cell suspension carefully.
Resuspend cell suspension with 1 mL of 30% Percoll.
Add 4 mL of 30% Percoll on top of the resuspended cells.
Place an unflamed Pasteur pipet in each 15 mL tube, covering the top with a gloved finger while gently placing the tip to the bottom of the tube.
Underlay 4 mL of 70% Percoll by pipetting slowly in 1 mL increments into the open top of the Pasteur pipet.
Lift the tip of the Pasteur pipet very slightly off the bottom of the tube to release any last fluid and cover the top with a finger, then pull up carefully without disturbing the layers.
Centrifuge at 340 × g for 20 min at 23°C with acceleration of 2 and no brake.
Remove tubes from centrifuge very gently so as not to disturb the gradients.
Bring all tubes back to the cell culture hood at ~20°C–25°C.
Aspirate out the top 1 mL of liquid.
Slowly pipet 70% Percoll into a Pasteur pipet placed under the 30% Percoll layer.
Release the 70% Percoll slowly to form an interface with the 30% Percoll.
Cover the Pasteur pipet with finger and gently remove it.
Pipette out the interphase cells in 1 mL increments four times (total of 4 mL).
Transfer the collected 4 mL containing the cell layer into new labeled 15 mL tubes.
Use a circular pipetting method to avoid picking up unwanted 30% Percoll.
Fill a 15 mL tube up to 15 mL volume with Post-Percoll Solution.
Centrifuge the filled tube for 10 minutes at 300 × g, 4°C, max acceleration, and max brake.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged tube.
Re-suspend pellets with 90 μL MACS buffer and 10 μL CD11b microbeads.
Incubate on ice for 15 minutes.
Add 1 mL of MACS Buffer to samples.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Set up sorting columns in the tissue culture hood.
Place LS Columns tightly in the magnet and position them over opened 15 mL tubes.
Prewash each column with 3 mL of MACS Buffer through nylon filter.
Pre-wet each filter by adding 1 mL of HBSS to the middle of the filter and then dragging it to the side.
Remove samples from centrifuge, aspirate supernatant, and resuspend pellets in 500 μL of MACS Buffer.
Add cell suspension to nylon filter, rinse old tube with 2 mL of MACS Buffer, and add it to the filter.
Add 3 mL of MACS Buffer to column.
Remove “-” tubes once liquid has finished flowing through the columns and place them on ice.
Remove columns from magnet and place them on top of “+” tubes for collecting CD11b positive cells.
Mix 5 mL of MACS Buffer with each column using a serological pipette.
Plunge the column as hard as possible using the supplied plunger.
Repeat the process to add another 5 mL of MACS Buffer for each column, totaling 10 mL per column.
Place “+” tubes on ice alongside “-” tubes.
Once wash has flowed through the columns, carefully remove LS columns from the Magnetic MACS MultiStand and place them onto the “+” tubes.
Dab the top of the “-” tube on the bottom of the LS column to collect any liquid containing negative flowthrough cells before removal.
Centrifuge the samples for 10 minutes at 300 × g, 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from all tubes carefully, ensuring no bubbles are left behind, especially in the “+” tubes.
Resuspend the pellet in 400 μL of ice-cold 1X PBS.
Transfer the 400 μL of cell resuspension to fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Rinse the old 15 mL tube with 800 μL of 1X PBS and add this rinse to the new 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove supernatant and resuspend in media of choice.
